newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Kerry shares jump 25 pence to 650.
newsitem.headline: Kerry shares jump 25 pence to 650.

text.p: Shares in Kerry Group surged by 25 Irish pence to 650 on Friday with pent-up demand for the tightly-held stock driving the price higher, dealers said.
"The market is very firm and Kerry is a very illiquid stock," one dealer said.
By 1430 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish share was up 21.29 points to 2,645.67 with most of the leading industrial stocks benefiting from the firm tone.
Traders said Kerry's share price may have also received a fillip from rumours that Kerry was on the brink of selling DCA's bakery equipment business Bakers Aid.
"There have been rumours going around that Kerry was selling the doughnut-making division of the U.S. unit DCA," a trader said.

Kerry originally planed to sell Bakers Aid and use the proceeds to reduce its debt but announced in August that it was unhappy with the prices offered for the business and planned to develop Bakers Aid itself.
A Kerry spokesman was not immediately available for comment on the rumours.
